messages.content: The crash is in `priorityName`, which indexes `priorityNames[p-1]`. A stored priority of -1 gives index -2. The only writer is `createReminder`, which rejects priorities above 3 but never rejects values below 1. I'll write a reproducer that sends a negative priority.

function.name: code_patch

messages.content: The reproducer fails on the current code: negative priorities are accepted, and the list then returns 500. Now the fix, at the point where the value is accepted.
All tests pass. I'll file the issue for this cause.

function.arguments:
{"title": "createReminder accepts negative priority, so priorityName panics on GET /v1/reminders", "body": "Fingerprint fp_9fdb76. Reports: cr_ef6062 (x2) and cr_c603e6 (x1), all in v1.4.0 (commit 9c41e7a). Panic: runtime error: index out of range [-2] in api.priorityName (api/reminders.go), reached from viewOf, listReminders and getReminder.

Cause: createReminder (api/reminders.go:39) only rejected priority > 3. A request with "priority":-1 or -2 was stored as is. priorityName then indexes priorityNames[p-1], which is out of range for p <= 0 other than 0. Every later read of that reminder panics, so GET /v1/reminders for that user fails with a 500.

Fix: the create handler now rejects priority < 1 or > 3 with 400, which matches the documented 1 (high), 2 (normal), 3 (low). Reproducer: api/priority_test.go TestCreatePriorityOutOfRange. It failed on the old code (201 for -1 and -2, then 500 on list) and passes now.

Side effect: an explicit "priority":0 is now also refused with 400. Before, it was stored as 0 and shown as normal. Omitting the field still means normal.", "fingerprint": "fp_9fdb76", "reproducer": {"file": "api/priority_test.go", "function": "TestCreatePriorityOutOfRange"}, "root_cause": {"file": "api/reminders.go", "function": "(*API).createReminder"}}
